rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for gently caressing someone or an animal with the hand.

example.english: I gently stroke the cat's head.
example.jyutping: ngo5 hing1 hing1 mo1 zyu6 zek3 maau1 ge3 tau4

rows.note: Use this when a hand, brush, or broom is moved lightly across a surface in one direction rather than caressing it.

example.english: I stroke the broom lightly across the floor.
example.traditional: 我用掃把輕輕掃過地板。
example.jyutping: ngo5 jung6 sou3 baa2 hing1 hing1 sou3 gwo3 dei6 baan2

rows.note: Use this for the medical condition involving interrupted blood flow to the brain.

example.english: Grandpa suddenly had a stroke yesterday and is still in hospital.
example.traditional: 爺爺噚日突然中風，依家仲喺醫院留醫。
example.jyutping: je4 je2 cam4 jat6 dat6 jin4 zung3 fung1 ji1 gaa1 zung6 hai2 ji1 jyun2 lau4 ji1

rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial noun for a physical blow or hit.

example.english: He silenced the whole room with one stroke on the table.
example.traditional: 佢一嘢打落張枱，成間房都靜晒。
example.jyutping: keoi5 jat1 je5 daa2 lok6 zoeng1 toi2 seng4 gaan1 fong4 dou1 zing6 saai3

rows.note: Use this when referring to a particular swimming style such as butterfly or breaststroke.

example.english: This swimming stroke is not tiring even after swimming for a long time.
example.traditional: 呢種泳式游耐咗都唔攰。
example.jyutping: ni1 zung2 wing6 sik1 jau4 noi6 zo2 dou1 m4 gui6
